title: Courier Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: Set the courier inspection scope, test readiness and requirement-level evidence, contain deficiencies, authorize status, and preserve qualified closeout.
description: An original, fillable courier inspection checklist form for controlling time-critical document or parcel consignment through inspection checklist identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use when a courier dispatcher or qualified inspector must evaluate time-critical document or parcel consignment against the dispatch order, tracking record, and custody manifest and provide a traceable basis for release, restriction, hold, correction, or rejection.

sections.title: Courier inspection scope, criteria, and readiness
sections.guidance: Define the exact population and review basis so inspection conclusions remain bounded.

fields.label: Dispatch Order, Tracking Record, And Custody Manifest

blocks.label: Courier readiness verification
items: Named pickup and recipient contacts match the dispatch instruction
Each envelope, parcel, pouch, or seal has a unique manifest identity
Ready time, delivery deadline, and permitted intermediate stops are explicit
Courier identity, vehicle or route, and communication method are assigned
Signature, identification, chain-of-custody, or photo proof is specified
Secure pouch, tamper seal, orientation, and environmental controls are available
Building access, security desk, floor, and after-hours instructions are confirmed
Refusal, unreachable contact, and return-to-sender routing are defined
blocks.guidance: A failed readiness item must be resolved, excluded with rationale, or carried into the exception section.

sections.title: Courier requirement-level inspection results
sections.guidance: Record actual observations against explicit criteria and identify the evidence for each result.

blocks.label: Courier detailed inspection points
items: Dispatch number and tracking identity agree across label and manifest
Piece count and package identifiers agree with the pickup record
Tamper seal, pouch closure, and package surfaces show no unexplained change
Recipient name and acceptable alternate recipient rules are explicit
Required delivery deadline and escalation trigger are visible
Courier can preserve custody through access screening or security handoff
No prohibited or undeclared contents are apparent under applicable policy
Tracking scan can be captured at pickup, transfer, attempt, and delivery
Proof method protects confidential information unrelated to the delivery
Any seal, identity, count, deadline, or access discrepancy is stopped and routed
blocks.guidance: Checkboxes indicate that the point was examined; the result table carries findings and evidence.

sections.title: Courier measurements and evidence package
sections.guidance: Preserve readings, instruments, identity, and evidence needed to reproduce the inspection decision.

blocks.label: Measurement, count, or verification log
blocks.guidance: Use the method applicable to Manifested and accepted pieces and Seal, envelope, and parcel condition.

blocks.label: Available inspection evidence
items: Dispatch acceptance timestamp
Pickup scan and sender handoff confirmation
Seal or pouch identity image
Courier location or milestone timestamp
Security desk or controlled transfer record
Recipient identity method and signature reference
Attempt, refusal, or return scan
Final tracking and custody reconciliation

blocks.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

fields.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

sections.title: Courier exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Courier exception indicators
items: Sender is not ready at committed pickup time
Envelope, parcel, pouch, or seal identity differs from manifest
Package condition suggests opening, tampering, or damage
Courier cannot access the pickup or delivery control point
Named recipient or permitted alternate is unavailable
Delivery deadline is at risk or missed
Security screening conflicts with handling instruction
Tracking scan or signature capture is unavailable
Unplanned custody transfer or vehicle change is required
Sender, recipient, or dispatcher disputes the recorded piece count
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Courier inspection status and release decision
sections.guidance: Do not turn a checklist score into release when a critical exception or evidence gap remains.

sections.title: Courier inspection checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: Use this courier inspection checklist with the applicable customer commitment, carrier terms, site policy, and retention requirements. Do not infer acceptance or release from a signature alone; unresolved identity, count, condition, custody, or proof issues require an owner, escalation, and documented disposition.

blocks.label: Prepared, reviewed, and accepted
blocks.guidance: A signature records accountability for the stated decision; it does not cure missing evidence or override a stop condition.
